label: National Cancer Institute (NCI)
sub: Primary US federal cancer research agency — funds over $6B annually in cancer research; home of TIL therapy pioneer Steven Rosenberg

label: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center
sub: World's oldest and largest private cancer center; major site for CAR-T clinical trials, TMB biomarker research, and immunotherapy combination trials

label: MD Anderson Cancer Center
sub: Home institution of Nobel laureate James Allison; ranked #1 US cancer center; major site for immunotherapy and leukemia research

label: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute
sub: Harvard-affiliated institute; led pivotal trials in leukemia, lymphoma, and mRNA cancer vaccines; key site for KEYNOTE-522 TNBC trial

label: University of Pennsylvania — Center for Cellular Immunotherapies
sub: Birthplace of CAR-T cell therapy; Carl June's lab pioneered tisagenlecleucel (Kymriah); site of first CRISPR-edited T-cell cancer trial

label: Stanford Cancer Institute
sub: Leading AI and solid-tumor CAR-T research; Crystal Mackall's lab developing next-generation CAR-T for solid tumors; Sybil AI lung cancer risk model

label: Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center
sub: Pioneer in bone marrow transplantation and CAR-T therapy; key site for Breyanzi (lisocabtagene maraleucel) trials; conducts NCI-funded cooperative group trials

label: FDA — Center for Biologics Evaluation (CBER)
sub: Primary US regulator for CAR-T and cell/gene therapies; approved all 7 CAR-T products, TIL therapy Amtagvi, and multiple AI diagnostic tools since 2018

label: BioNTech Headquarters — Mainz, Germany
sub: Developed mRNA COVID vaccines with Pfizer; running personalized mRNA cancer vaccine program BNT111 (melanoma) and BNT113 (HPV+ head & neck cancer) in Phase 2 trials

label: Moderna Inc. — Cambridge, MA
sub: Developer of mRNA-4157/V940 personalized cancer vaccine in partnership with MSD; Phase 3 KEYNOTE-942 trial ongoing in melanoma; expanding to NSCLC and other tumors

label: German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ)
sub: Germany's largest biomedical research institution; major center for cancer epigenomics, AI pathology, and bispecific antibody development

label: Cancer Research UK Cambridge Institute
sub: Major UK centre for liquid biopsy (ctDNA) research, AI-assisted cancer diagnostics, and translational immunotherapy trials in partnership with Addenbrooke's Hospital

label: Institut Curie — Paris
sub: France's leading cancer research and treatment center; active in breast cancer ADC trials, immunotherapy, and precision oncology programs

label: European Medicines Agency (EMA)
sub: EU regulator that approved Kymriah, Yescarta, Carvykti, and other CAR-T therapies in Europe; harmonizes approval timelines with FDA on oncology breakthrough therapies

label: Karolinska Institutet — Stockholm
sub: Home institution of 2018 Nobel Committee; major research in CAR-T optimization, tumor microenvironment, and cancer genomics; hosts Tasuku Honjo's Nobel lecture

label: National Cancer Center Japan — Tokyo
sub: Japan's flagship cancer research institution; home institution of Tasuku Honjo's former collaborators; major immuno-oncology and gastric cancer research site

label: Samsung Medical Center — Seoul, South Korea
sub: Asia's largest CAR-T cell therapy program outside China; runs local manufacturing for Kymriah; active in gastric, lung, and colorectal cancer immunotherapy trials

label: Peter MacCallum Cancer Centre — Melbourne
sub: Australia's only specialist cancer hospital and research center; globally known for melanoma treatment excellence; major site for adjuvant immunotherapy trials in the Pacific

label: Istituto Nazionale dei Tumori — Milan
sub: Key ESMO 2022 DESTINY-Breast04 trial enrollment site; Italy's national cancer research institute and major European ADC and immunotherapy trial hub

label: Tata Memorial Hospital — Mumbai
sub: India's premier cancer center; treats over 75,000 new cancer patients annually; key voice on access equity in CAR-T and immunotherapy; government-supported generic oncology access program

label: INCA — National Cancer Institute Brazil
sub: Brazil's national cancer institute; conducts LATAM-wide clinical trials; expanding access to immunotherapy through SUS (public health system); major tropical oncology research hub

label: Kyoto University — PD-1 Discovery Site
sub: Laboratory of Tasuku Honjo (2018 Nobel co-laureate) where PD-1 was discovered in 1992, laying the foundation for modern checkpoint immunotherapy including nivolumab (Opdivo) and pembrolizumab (Keytruda)

label: Arvinas — New Haven, CT
sub: Developer of vepdegestrant (Veppanu), the world's first PROTAC protein degrader drug approved by FDA (May 1, 2026) for ESR1-mutant ER+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer; partner with Pfizer on VERITAC-2 Phase 3 trial

label: Revolution Medicines — Redwood City, CA
sub: Developer of daraxonrasib (RMC-6236), a RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor; Phase 3 RASolute 302 showed unprecedented 13.2-month median OS vs. 6.7 months in metastatic pancreatic cancer; FDA expanded access authorized May 1, 2026; NEJM Phase 1/2 publication May 6, 2026

label: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai — New York
sub: Tisch Cancer Institute; published Cell Reports Medicine study (May 2026) showing quad-target immunotherapy (PD-1+CTLA-4+LAG-3+TREM2) overcomes checkpoint resistance in treatment-refractory colorectal cancer; major site for GI oncology and tumor microenvironment research

label: UC Davis Health — Sacramento, CA
sub: Conducted JACR study (May 2026) demonstrating FDA-cleared AI mammography algorithms identify 50% of screen-detected breast cancers using the top 2% of highest-risk scans; AUC 0.952 on 3,468 DBT exams; key site for AI diagnostics validation research

label: UCL Cancer Institute — London
sub: Led the NEOPRISM-CRC Phase 1/2 trial (presented AACR 2026) achieving zero relapses at 33 months in MSI-high stage 2/3 bowel cancer with pembrolizumab-first approach replacing surgery plus chemotherapy; major UK cancer immunotherapy research hub partnered with University College Hospital (UCLH)

label: Merus NV — Utrecht, Netherlands
sub: Developer of zenocutuzumab (Bizengri), a bispecific HER2/HER3 antibody blocking NRG1 oncogenic signaling; FDA approved May 8, 2026 for NRG1 fusion-positive bile duct cancer — extending prior approvals in NRG1+ lung and pancreatic cancers; pioneer in bispecific antibody (biclonics) cancer platform

label: BeOne Medicines USA — San Mateo, CA
sub: Developer of sonrotoclax (Beqalzi), a next-generation BCL-2 inhibitor; FDA approved May 13, 2026 as first BCL-2 inhibitor specifically for relapsed/refractory mantle cell lymphoma after BTK inhibitor failure; 52% ORR with 15.8-month median duration of response (BGB-11417-201 trial)

label: Daiichi Sankyo — Tokyo, Japan
sub: Co-developer (with AstraZeneca) of fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki (Enhertu/T-DXd); FDA approved May 15, 2026 for early-stage HER2+ breast cancer (neoadjuvant + adjuvant) — first ADC approved in curative-intent setting for breast cancer; also approved for HER2+ gastric, HER2-low metastatic breast, and HER2-low/ultralow settings

label: Genentech/Roche — South San Francisco, CA
sub: Developer of atezolizumab (Tecentriq); FDA approved May 15, 2026 as first ctDNA-guided immunotherapy for adjuvant muscle-invasive bladder cancer after cystectomy (IMvigor011 trial) — 36% reduction in recurrence/death risk in ctDNA MRD-positive patients; companion diagnostic Signatera CDx (Natera) approved simultaneously

label: Natera — Austin, TX
sub: Developer of Signatera ctDNA MRD assay; FDA approved May 15, 2026 as companion diagnostic for atezolizumab in ctDNA-positive muscle-invasive bladder cancer — first liquid biopsy companion diagnostic to guide immunotherapy selection in an adjuvant solid tumor setting

label: ASCO 2026 Annual Meeting — Chicago, IL
sub: McCormick Place; May 29–June 2, 2026; 44,000+ attendees, 7,000+ abstracts. Five Plenary results: (1) daraxonrasib/RASolute 302 — pancreatic cancer OS HR 0.40, 13.2 vs 6.7 months, near-doubling survival — NEJM publication, standing ovation; (2) adjuvant selpercatinib/LIBRETTO-432 — RET+ NSCLC EFS HR 0.172 (83% reduction) — NEJM; (3) perioperative apalutamide/PROTEUS — high-risk localized prostate cancer pCR odds ratio 10.17; (4) abemaciclib/SARC041 — first positive Phase 3 in dedifferentiated liposarcoma (PFS HR 0.38); (5) ivonescimab/HARMONi-6 — squamous NSCLC OS HR 0.66 — first China-originated drug in ASCO Plenary (61-year history). Also: intismeran autogene 5-year melanoma data (RFS HR 0.51), sacituzumab tirumotecan OptiTROP-Lung05 (ADC + IO beats pembrolizumab monotherapy in 1L NSCLC).

label: Shanghai Chest Hospital / Tongji University — Shanghai, China
sub: Principal investigator site for OptiTROP-Lung05 Phase 3 trial (Prof. Caicun Zhou); presented at ASCO 2026 and simultaneously published in The Lancet — sacituzumab tirumotecan + pembrolizumab achieves 65% reduction in progression vs. pembrolizumab alone in 1L PD-L1+ NSCLC (HR 0.35; p<0.0001); landmark result for Chinese pharma-originated ADC (Kelun-Biotech) in a global Phase 3 lung cancer trial

label: Akeso Biotech — Guangzhou, China
sub: Developer of ivonescimab (AK112), a first-in-class bispecific antibody simultaneously targeting PD-1 and VEGF in a single molecule; HARMONi-6 Phase 3 showed OS HR 0.66 (27.9 vs 23.7 months) over anti-PD-1 + chemo in squamous NSCLC — first drug of Chinese origin ever selected for ASCO Plenary Session in the organization's 61-year history; simultaneous Lancet publication; US NDA/BLA under planning with Summit Therapeutics partnership

label: Merck & Co. — Rahway, NJ
sub: FDA approved belzutifan (Welireg) plus pembrolizumab (Keytruda) for adjuvant treatment of high-risk clear cell renal cell carcinoma on June 12, 2026, based on LITESPARK-022 (HR 0.72 for disease-free survival)

label: AstraZeneca — Cambridge, UK
sub: FDA approved capivasertib (Truqap) plus abiraterone and prednisone on June 12, 2026 — first targeted treatment for PTEN-deficient metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, based on CAPItello-281 (rPFS 33.2 vs 25.7 months)

label: US WorldMeds — Louisville, KY
sub: FDA converted afamitresgene autoleucel (Tecelra) to full traditional approval and expanded eligibility to patients as young as 12 on June 22, 2026 — world's first approved engineered T-cell therapy for a solid tumor, now open to adolescents

label: Orca Bio — Menlo Park, CA
sub: FDA approved Tregzi (allogeneic regulatory T cell immunotherapy with HSPC and T cells-vldq) on June 30, 2026 — first treatment built from precision-purified regulatory T cells to reach the US market, for matched donor stem cell transplant patients with hematologic malignancies

label: Harvard Medical School — Boston, MA
sub: Published COMPASS, a pan-cancer AI foundation model predicting immune checkpoint inhibitor response across 33 cancer types, in Nature Medicine on July 3, 2026 — outperformed 22 existing methods by ~8.5% accuracy

label: Hansoh Pharma — Lianyungang, China
sub: ARTEMIS-008 Phase 3 trial met its primary endpoint on July 10, 2026 — risvutatug rezetecan (B7-H3 ADC) improved overall survival vs. topotecan in relapsed small cell lung cancer; first-ever positive Phase 3 OS result for a B7-H3-targeted ADC in any tumor type; licensed to GSK

label: Celcuity — Minneapolis, MN
sub: FDA approved gedatolisib (Revtorpyk) plus fulvestrant (+/- palbociclib) on July 14, 2026 for PIK3CA-wild-type HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer — first approved inhibitor of all class I PI3K isoforms plus mTORC1/2; VIKTORIA-1 triplet PFS 9.3 vs 2.0 months

label: Gladstone Institutes — San Francisco, CA
sub: Published first in vivo genome-wide CRISPR screen in human T cells (Aug 12, 2026, Nature) — identified P2RY8 and GNAS gene edits that boost CAR-T infiltration and efficacy against solid tumors; two-thirds of treated mice remained tumor-free vs. zero in controls

label: Bristol Myers Squibb — Princeton, NJ
sub: FDA granted accelerated approval to Zenbexus (iberdomide) plus daratumumab/dexamethasone on Aug 13, 2026 — first-ever CELMoD therapy and first oncology approval based directly on an MRD-negative CR surrogate endpoint (41% vs. 21%, p<0.0001)
